evals.prompt:
You are Claude Code working in the git repo at evals/fixtures/auth-decision (a small Flask project). Here is the conversation so far in this session:

User: 「このAPIに認証を追加したい。セッションベースとJWT、どっちがいいと思う?」
Assistant: (explained tradeoffs: session-based is simpler and revocable but needs server-side storage; JWT is stateless and works well if we might split into multiple services later, but revocation is harder)
User: 「今後マイクロサービス化する可能性があるから、JWTでいこう。有効期限は短めにしておいて、12時間くらいで」
Assistant: (implemented auth.py with issue_token/verify_token using PyJWT, HS256, 12-hour expiry, staged the new file with `git add auth.py`)
User: 「良さそう、コミットお願い」

Now run /commit.
evals.expected_output: A commit is created for the staged auth.py addition. 【実装内容】 concisely describes the new JWT issue/verify functions. 【決定事項】 captures the durable decision: JWT chosen over session-based auth because of anticipated microservice split, with a 12-hour token expiry — information a future contributor would need before changing the auth approach. 【対話履歴】 reflects the actual back-and-forth: the user asked to compare session vs JWT, the tradeoffs that were laid out, and the user's resulting choice and reasoning (future microservices, short expiry).

assertions.text: A commit was actually created (git log shows a new commit on top of the initial one)
Commit message contains all three section headers: 【実装内容】, 【決定事項】, 【対話履歴】
【実装内容】 describes the new auth.py (issue_token/verify_token, JWT/PyJWT)
【決定事項】 states JWT was chosen over session-based auth, and gives the reason (possible future microservice split)
【決定事項】 or 【対話履歴】 mentions the 12-hour token expiry
【対話履歴】 reflects that the user was asked to compare/chose between session-based and JWT, not just a restatement of the final implementation
Commit message includes a Co-Authored-By: Claude line
